claim: The cohort was 12,103 FFPE samples from 1454 sequencing batches run in one laboratory on TSO500 with two NextSeq 550Dx and one NovaSeq 6000Dx, March 2020 to December 2024.
quote: The data set includes 12,103 sequencing formalin-fixed, paraffinembedded samples from 1454 sequencing batches used in a single laboratory with a standardized clinical protocol using the TruSight Oncology 500 (TSO500) DNA/RNA kit and two NextSeq 550Dx and one NovaSeq 6000Dx (Illumina, San Diego, CA).

claim: A gene was called batch-affected when normalized MAD of fold change was <0.25 and median fold change was <0.75 or >1.25 within a batch.
quote: A batch effect was considered to cause a common foldchange shift in a specific gene across samples within a batch if mad/mFC was <0.25 and mFC was <0.75 or >1.25

claim: Two-dimensional kernel density estimation put the 95th highest density region at mFC 0.801 to 1.217 and mad/mFC up to 0.2499; the 0.75/1.25 and 0.25 cutoffs were chosen to sit just outside that boundary.
quote: The 95th highest density region spanned mFC values of 0.801 to 1.217 and mad/mFC values up to 0.2499 (Supplemental Table S1); the fold-change cutoffs of 0.75 and 1.25 and the mad/mFC threshold of 0.25 were selected to fall outside this boundary and within the 95th to 99th percentile range.

claim: Copy number theory at 50% representative tumor purity independently yields fold changes of 0.75 and 1.25 for hemizygous deletion and single-copy gain, validating the empirical cutoffs.
quote: yields fold-change values of 0.75 and 1.25, respectively, confirming that the selected thresholds correspond to biologically meaningful copy number states.

claim: MAD was divided by the median because MAD scales with the median.
quote: However, because MAD values tend to scale with the median, MAD was normalized by dividing it by the median to reduce this dependency (Supplemental Figure S2).

claim: MAD was added as a second metric to find genes with low intrabatch variability, because true homozygous deletions or amplifications also occur in specific genes.
quote: Given that true-positive events, such as homozygous deletions or amplifications, can occur in specific genes, MAD was incorporated as an additional metric to identify genes with low intrabatch variability.

claim: Change point detection used a rolling mean over a sliding window of five consecutive batches.
quote: A rolling mean was calculated using a sliding window of five consecutive batches.

claim: A moving-average PR score of 99.0 was the alert criterion, i.e. at least 1% below the 100% maximum pass rate.
quote: A moving average threshold of 99.0 for the PRb score was applied as an alert criterion, corresponding to a deviation of at least 1% from the maximum pass rate (100%).

claim: Sorting median fold change of target genes within one real-world batch showed some genes past the mutation-detection threshold.
quote: When sorting the mFC of target genes obtained from samples within a specific real-world sequencing batch, some genes exceeded the threshold used for mutation detection

claim: Certain genes were recurrently affected during specific periods, implicating external factors.
quote: affected during specific periods, suggesting that external factors may contribute to these variations

claim: HIST1H3A, NOTCH1, MCL1 and ZBTB7A showed high or low mFC in >10% of batches regardless of batch.
quote: Notably, genes such as HIST1H3A, NOTCH1, MCL1, and ZBTB7A consistently exhibited >10% frequency across multiple sequencing batches with either high or low mFC, regardless of the batch itself

claim: Deviations of recurrently shifted genes were spread across the whole sequencing timeline, not confined to one time frame.
quote: Temporal analysis of genes with recurrently elevated or suppressed mFC values revealed that these deviations were not confined to a particular time frame but were distributed across the entire sequencing timeline

claim: Change point detection flagged genes with aberrant fold-change patterns across at least three consecutive batches.
quote: change point detection analysis was applied to identify genes with aberrant fold change patterns across at least three consecutive sequencing batches

claim: 52 genes carried recurrent mFC shifts across the cohort.
quote: This analysis uncovered 52 genes with recurrent mFC shifts across the cohort

claim: The 52 genes split into persistently affected genes and genes deviating only during specific time intervals.
quote: allowing classification into distinct patterns, those persistently affected and those showing deviations only during specific time intervals

claim: mFC was significantly shifted during affected periods in 51 of 52 genes (FDR<0.05): 14 gain-direction, 37 loss-direction.
quote: mFC values were significantly elevated or reduced during affected periods in 51 of 52 genes (false discovery rate <0.05), with 14 genes showing copy number gain-direction shifts and 37 showing loss-direction shifts.

claim: mad/mFC did not differ significantly between affected and unaffected periods in 44 of 52 genes, so intrabatch variability stayed stable.
quote: in most genes (44 of 52, false discovery rate ≥0.05), indicating that intrabatch variability remained stable regardless of batch-effect status

claim: Systematic mFC deviation with preserved intrabatch consistency marks batch-level technical bias, not recurrent somatic CNA.
quote: This systematic mFC deviation with preserved intrabatch consistency pattern was characteristic of batch-level technical bias rather than recurrent somatic copy number alterations.

claim: MMRD pathway genes stayed inside the stable range across all sequencing runs.
quote: demonstrated that mFC values for MMRD pathway genes remained within the predefined stable range (mFC 0.75 to 1.25; mad/mFC ≤ 0.25) across all sequencing runs, indicating no evidence of systematic batch-associated bias affecting MMRD-related gene coverage

claim: HR-related genes CHEK1 and PALB2 showed significant batch-associated copy number loss during specific periods.
quote: significant batch-associated copy number loss was observed in the HR-related genes CHEK1 and PALB2 during specific periods

claim: HR gene loss is a key biomarker for PARP inhibitor eligibility, so artifactual HRD calls carry therapeutic consequences.
quote: This finding is particularly concerning because the loss of HR genes serves as a key biomarker for determining eligibility for poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase inhibitor therapy.

claim: In a 16-sample batch, ARID1A fell below the 0.75 deletion threshold in 11 of 16 samples (68.75%), and 9 (56.25%) below the gene-specific 0.656 cutoff.
quote: In a representative batch containing 16 samples, ARID1A exhibited fold-change values below the mFC deletion threshold of 0.75 in 11 of 16 samples (68.75%), with 9 samples (56.25%) further falling below the gene-specific deletion cutoff of 0.656 defined by the TSO500 secondary analysis pipeline.

claim: In the same batch MCL1 exceeded the 1.25 gain threshold in 13 of 16 samples (81.25%), with 3 (18.75%) above the gene-specific 1.624 cutoff.
quote: Conversely, MCL1 displayed fold-change values above the general copy gain threshold of 1.25 in 13 of 16 samples (81.25%), with 3 samples (18.75%) additionally exceeding the gene-specific gain cutoff of 1.624

claim: Deviations were more pronounced when the gene, cytoband, arm or whole chromosome showed consistent copy number change.
quote: In cases where the affected gene, its cytoband, chromosomal arm, or entire chromosome exhibited consistent copy number changes, the deviation was more

claim: Batch-level mFC is shown as a reference value alongside observed fold changes, with no automated correction applied.
quote: the mFC is provided as a reference value alongside the observed fold changes of genes exceeding both the mFC and mad/mFC thresholds, allowing interpreters to contextualize potential deviations and distinguish true copy number events from batch-associated bias without applying automated correction

claim: The PR score is the proportion of genes exceeding both thresholds over the total target genes, a single-value batch screen.
quote: batch-level bias was summarized as a PR score, defined as the proportion of genes exceeding both thresholds relative to the total number of target genes

claim: Batch effects manifested in two forms: sudden deviations at a specific time point, and recurrent persistent biases spanning many batches.
quote: These artifacts were found to manifest in two major forms: sudden deviations associated with reagent or equipment issues confined to a specific time point (Figure 1B); and recurrent, persistent biases spanning multiple batches, likely reflecting long-term technical or procedural variations

claim: Limitation: one institutional data set and one sequencing panel; generalizability needs external validation.
quote: First, the analysis was based on a single institutional data set and a single sequencing panel, and external validation across institutions and platforms will be needed to establish generalizability.

claim: Limitation: recurrent tumor alterations shared across a batch (7+/10-, 1p/19q, 3q26-qter) can shift the batch median and cause misclassification.
quote: Well-known events, such as chromosome 7+/10− in high-grade gliomas, 1p/19q codeletions in oligodendrogliomas, and 3q26-qter gains in squamous cell carcinomas, may shift the batch-level median, thereby introducing systematic misclassification.

claim: Limitation: no orthogonal validation by FISH, SNP array or immunohistochemistry.
quote: Third, orthogonal validation using independent methods, such as fluorescence in situ hybridization, single-nucleotide polymorphism array, or immunohistochemistry, was not performed to formally confirm the batch-associated nature of the flagged copy number deviations.

claim: True events were separated from artifacts by absence of clinically suspected alterations on routine diagnostics plus concurrent involvement of multiple genes in one batch.
quote: The distinction between true copy number events and batch-associated artifacts was instead inferred from the absence of clinically suspected alterations in the relevant genes through routine diagnostic evaluation, and from the concurrent involvement of multiple genes within the same batch, suggesting a systematic rather than tumor-specific origin.

claim: Limitation: the framework was not benchmarked against PCA- or SVD-based batch-effect detection.
quote: effect detection strategies, such as PCA- or SVD-based approaches, was not performed, and future studies should benchmark the proposed framework against existing methods to better establish its relative utility.

claim: Batch effects could not be attributed to specific experimental factors because prospective lot-level records were absent; temporal clustering suggests episodic upstream changes.
quote: Although the present study could not directly attribute observed batch effects to specific experimental factors because of the absence of prospective lot-level records, the temporal clustering of affected batches suggests episodic changes in upstream experimental conditions as plausible contributing factors.

claim: Recommendation: CNV results deposited in public repositories such as cBioPortal should carry batch identifiers and batch-level mFC metrics.
quote: it is recommended that CNV results submitted to public repositories, such as cBioPortal, should include batch identifiers and batch-level mFC metrics.

claim: Thresholds are adjustable: lower-purity cohorts may need more permissive fold-change boundaries, higher-purity cohorts more stringent ones.
quote: Laboratories operating with cohorts of systematically lower purity may require more permissive foldchange boundaries, whereas those with higher purity samples may apply more stringent cutoffs.
